name: Political moderate
summary: A political moderate rejects radical or extreme views and seeks a position between the main poles, usually through compromise, gradual reform and attention to the merits of each issue. Moderation is a stance about method and range more than a fixed program, so moderates hold mixed positions that vary by country, and in practice they support democratic institutions, a mixed economy with a welfare state, and coalition-building across left and right.
scope: The generic moderate or centrist stance as documented in Wikipedia's articles on moderates and centrism (the Doctrinaires, Whigs, Christian Democracy and Third Way strands), the classical argument for the mean and the middle class in Aristotle's Politics IV, and the scholarship on moderation as an ideology of the middle. It excludes any particular party and the more programmatic strands, which have their own profiles (centrism, radical centrism, liberal centrism). Because the label is positional, many answers are low-confidence inferences about issues on which moderates divide.

keyFigures.name: Aristotle
keyFigures.role: Early theorist of the mean and of the middle class as the basis of a stable constitution

keyFigures.name: François Guizot
keyFigures.role: Leader of the French Doctrinaires, named in the centrism article as a 19th-century centrist

sources.title: Moderate

sources.title: Centrism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Centrist support for gradual change, welfare-state programs, coalitions, European integration and Third Way pragmatism.

sources.title: Politics, Book IV (trans. Jowett)
sources.author: Aristotle
sources.usedFor: The argument that the mean and the middle class give the best and most stable constitution, mixed between few and many.

sources.author: Ido de Haan and Matthijs Lok
sources.usedFor: Moderation as an ideology of the middle or third way, and its relation to compromise in deep conflicts.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Centrist welfare-state support is documented, but moderates split on how far the state should provide care versus mix in private insurance, so only a mild lean is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Moderates accept some redistribution but avoid "substantial" shifts either way; no source gives a moderate position on wage floors, so this is treated as split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Centrism is described as blending market-friendly ideas with social programs, so a moderate neither endorses markets over government outright nor rejects them.

public-ownership.rationale: Centrists back welfare-state programs and a mixed economy but are not described as favoring broad public ownership of industry, which is a sweeping change.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Moderates support some redistribution while resisting drastic measures; "significantly higher" is a strong version, so adherents split.

unions-good.rationale: Centrist parties accommodate both labor and business; a mild positive view of unions is inferred, not documented directly.

property-fundamental.rationale: Centrism opposes abolishing existing classes yet is not tied to a strong property-rights doctrine, so moderates split on how inviolable property should be.

regulate-corporations.rationale: A moderate seeks balance between market freedom and oversight; whether regulation should be tighter depends on the case, so no consistent lean.

cut-welfare.rationale: Centrists are described as supporting welfare-state programs, so they reject cutting them on the dependency argument, though many favor reform.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is a structural economic change at odds with gradual reform within a mixed economy; inferred, not stated.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Moderates weigh security against liberty without a doctrinal answer, so adherents are genuinely split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is not a defining moderate issue and the label spans views on both sides of this question.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Moderates have no stated doctrine on speech limits; they are divided between free-speech and protection concerns.

strong-leader.rationale: Moderation is defined by rejecting extremes and favoring compromise, which cuts against a leader bypassing gridlock and institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Rejecting radical or extreme views includes rejecting anarchist abolition of the state, which moderates see as an extreme position.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun policy splits self-described moderates, who tend to favor some regulation without strict limits; no source settles it.

empower-police-military.rationale: No documented moderate stance; moderates tend to favor balance between security and civil liberties.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A culturally contested issue on which moderates divide rather than share a position.

decide-locally.rationale: Centrism is not tied to either centralization or localism; moderates accept both depending on context.

rehabilitation.rationale: Moderates generally want a mix of punishment and rehabilitation; the statement frames them as alternatives, so split.

traditional-family.rationale: Moderates sit between traditionalist and progressive views on family; no source assigns a position.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social liberalism is paired with centrist economics in the centrism article, and moderates on average lean toward legalization, though some are cautious.

abortion-legal.rationale: Moderates typically accept legal abortion in most cases with some limits; this is an inference from the moderate middle on social issues, not stated.

more-religion-public.rationale: Historic liberal centrism opposed clericalism, so a mild disagreement is inferred for moderates.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Moderates endorse equal treatment but differ on active corrective measures; no stated moderate position.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A contested academic claim with no moderate doctrine; moderates avoid taking the strongest side.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Moderates sit between cosmopolitan and nationalist poles; no source indicates a view.

gradual-change.rationale: Centrists are documented as supporting gradual change within a political system, and Wikipedia's centrism notes prudence when enacting change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration divides moderates and centrist parties; a middle position leaves this statement split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Centrists have backed European integration, but moderates generally do not endorse transferring more power to the UN; split.

free-trade.rationale: Third Way centrism blends market-friendly ideas, supporting openness to trade, though moderates acknowledge costs to some workers.

nation-first.rationale: Moderates avoid both nationalist and globalist extremes; the statement poses a pole and gets a split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Moderates are divided on intervention and no source gives a shared position.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders is a radical goal; moderates reject extreme positions and favor managed immigration.

limit-growth.rationale: Degrowth is a radical position; moderates favor reconciling growth and environmental protection.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Moderates accept climate concerns but prefer incremental measures to drastic ones, so this word choice yields a split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Neither techno-optimism nor skepticism is a moderate commitment; split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No documented moderate position; moderates divide on nuclear energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Moderation is defined by rejection of radical and extreme means, and moderates prefer reform within a political system.

experts-over-public.rationale: Moderates value pragmatism and expertise but also democratic legitimacy; split between them.

central-planning.rationale: A fully planned economy is an extreme alternative to the mixed economy centrists favor.

socialized-markets.rationale: A moderate accepts markets and some public involvement, but this specific ownership condition is not a moderate doctrine.

land-value-tax.rationale: A specialist fiscal proposal with no moderate stance; moderates would not back replacing most taxes with a single tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Centrists accept some redistribution without abolishing wealth differences; "heavily" taxed is a stronger claim, so split.

basic-income.rationale: Basic income is neither standard centrist doctrine nor rejected by it; some moderates favor it, others prefer targeted welfare.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Third Way and centrist positions lean toward market openness rather than protectionism, though this is inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Directing investment is a strong interventionist stance; moderates favor a balanced mixed economy and market allocation within rules.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Aristotle's middle class favors broad moderate property holdings, but modern moderates have no stated position on ownership structure.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money and wage labor is a radical aim; moderates reject extreme views.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: An extreme free-market proposal that moderates reject as a radical departure from established institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Moderates accommodate both sides but not through state-recognized bodies setting wages and prices; inferred from the mixed economy.

one-party-rule.rationale: Centrism is described as strongest in multi-party systems working through coalitions, which is incompatible with single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Moderates are found in monarchies and republics; no stated position, so adherents are split.

democracy-best.rationale: Centrism is associated with democratic party systems and coalitions; moderates support democracy but may qualify "even when voters choose badly".

direct-votes.rationale: Moderates generally favor representative institutions and compromise over plebiscites; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Replacing parliaments with councils is a radical restructuring that moderates reject.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is a disruptive change; moderates generally favor existing institutions and negotiation.

natural-rulers.rationale: Aristotle's moderate polity rests on a broad middle class rather than natural rulers, and modern moderates accept democratic equality.

political-violence-never.rationale: Moderates reject extreme means, though few would say violence is never justified in any case.

war-builds-character.rationale: Glorifying war is an extreme position; moderates reject it.

separate-church-state.rationale: Liberal centrism historically opposed clericalism; most moderates favor separation though not strictly.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Basing laws on scripture is a religious extreme that moderates reject.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Private provision of courts and defense is an extreme libertarian proposal that moderates reject.

military-superiority.rationale: Moderates hold varied views on defense policy and no source gives a common position.

ethnic-nation.rationale: An ethnically homogeneous nation is an extreme ideal; moderates tend to reject it.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Moderates and centrists accommodate both sides and reject class conflict as the master explanation.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Centrists support some redistribution but not abolition of class differences, so equality of outcomes is too far.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Moderates endorse recognition of indigenous rights in general but vary on authority over land; split.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Moderates generally avoid sweeping reparations claims as a divisive measure; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political union of civilizations is a radical project and not a moderate aim.

self-interest-moral.rationale: A philosophical stance with no moderate doctrine; split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Moderates balance communal duty and individual rights rather than ranking them.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: A philosophical position not tied to moderation; adherents split.

limit-population.rationale: Active population limiting is a coercive policy that moderates reject, inferred from opposition to extremes.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: An extreme anti-industrial claim that moderates reject.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Speeding change regardless of disruption conflicts with the moderate preference for gradual change and prudence.

human-enhancement.rationale: No moderate doctrine; moderates divide on bodily autonomy versus caution.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Handing more government decisions to algorithms is a radical change at odds with gradualism; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Moderates weigh privacy and security, with no stated position.

restore-past-order.rationale: Restoring a lost order is a reactionary goal, an extreme in the moderate framing, and moderates favor pragmatic progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Third Way leaders described their approach as neither left nor right but pragmatic, and Wikipedia's moderate entry says moderation rejects ideological extremes.

direct-action.rationale: Moderates work through elections, parliaments and compromise instead of direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: A principle prominent in anarchist thought; moderates have no specific view.

return-to-foraging.rationale: An extreme anti-civilization proposal that moderates reject.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A radical utopian aim that moderates reject.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Centrists back welfare programs but also moderate redistribution, not full distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Replacing profit as the motive is a structural change beyond the centrist mixed economy; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Centrists accommodate both employers and workers; viewing profit as exploitation is a class-conflict claim they reject.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: An extreme revolutionary position that moderates reject.

collective-farming.rationale: Compulsory collectivization is an extreme measure that moderates reject.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A sweeping Marxist-Leninist claim; centrists accept capitalism within a regulated mixed economy.

taxation-theft.rationale: Centrists accept taxation funding welfare programs, so calling it theft is an extreme libertarian view.

harm-principle.rationale: Moderates are not committed to this specific liberal principle and accept additional paternalist or moral limits.

individual-rights-only.rationale: No documented moderate stance; moderates accept some group-based accommodation.

conscription.rationale: Moderates vary by country and no source gives a common stance.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Moderates are tied to democratic participation and coalitions, so exit as the main check is unlikely.

state-as-business.rationale: Third Way blended market ideas with the state, but citizens as customers is a stronger marketization than moderates endorse.

positive-liberty.rationale: Centrist liberalism includes social liberal strands that agree and market strands that do not; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: A populist elite-power claim that moderates are unlikely to share; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: An extreme claim that moderates reject.

organic-representation.rationale: Moderates support party-based democracy and coalitions rather than corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: The state directing all life is an extreme position that moderates reject.

national-rebirth.rationale: A radical national regeneration program is the kind of extreme moderates reject.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Expansionism is an extreme foreign policy that moderates reject.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal personal loyalty as authority is incompatible with the institutional, multi-party politics centrists operate in.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is an extreme social order that moderates reject.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: A radical epistemological claim not typical of moderates, who stress pragmatic evaluation on the merits.

universal-morality.rationale: A philosophical question with no moderate stance; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Centrism is defined by accommodating both sides and balancing interests through compromise, not by one common good worked out by reason.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A specific national question on which moderates have no shared position; split.

revive-national-language.rationale: No moderate stance; a specialist nationalist cause.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Moderates accept some worker voice but not a democratic vote on all company decisions; split.

school-vouchers.rationale: Third Way centrism mixed market and public provision; moderates are divided on vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Third Way politics is associated with balanced budgets, so a mild agreement is inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: Moderates value both economic and political freedoms but would not tie them so tightly; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Moderates rely on laws and institutions rather than rulers' example, inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: A generally accepted principle but moderates differ on its limits; no stated stance.

force-without-un.rationale: Moderates are split on unilateral force abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Moderate religious believers and secularists both call themselves moderate; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Moderates divide on this immigration-welfare question.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Third Way blended social programs with responsibility, and work requirements fit this approach, inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Centrist parties accommodate both sides, and Third Way thought favors cooperation between business and labor over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: An extreme iconoclastic proposal that moderates reject, favoring gradual change and institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: A confrontational anti-Western front is an extreme not typical of moderates.

workers-nation.rationale: No moderate stance; class-based national organization is not their framework.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Moderates lean toward equal treatment under law, though some retain traditional views.

ban-interest.rationale: Banning interest is a radical economic measure that moderates reject.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: An extreme position that moderates reject.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Moderates and centrists see the state as a forum for balancing interests and accommodating both sides, not a class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Moderates split between energy supply and environmental goals.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Moderates divide between integration and multiculturalism; no stated position.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim that moderates reject as extreme.

proportional-representation.rationale: Centrist parties do better under multi-party systems, but moderates are not unanimous on electoral reform.

national-mission.rationale: A missionary foreign policy is an extreme moderates are likely to avoid.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: A contested structural claim; moderates acknowledge inequality but do not share a theory.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Moderates generally work within institutions and avoid anti-establishment rhetoric, a feature of centrist populism not the mainstream.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic coercion is an extreme position that moderates reject.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Moderates have no stated position; they vary by context.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Centrists support welfare-state programs, so a minimal state is an extreme they reject.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: An extreme racist position that moderates reject.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Moderates reject extreme views and basic equal rights are a consensus point of mainstream democratic politics.

socialism-one-country.rationale: An internal Marxist debate on which moderates hold no position.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A contested characterization on which moderates have no shared position.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: No moderate stance; depends on national context.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Restricting religious conversion is an illiberal measure that moderates tend to reject.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religiously motivated ban that moderates are unlikely to endorse broadly.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Moderates are split between strict secular and accommodating approaches.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine alien to moderates, who oppose expanding state power on that logic.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Centrism is described in democratic multi-party and coalition terms, which assumes legitimacy from consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export aims are not part of centrist market-friendly thinking.

population-transfer.rationale: An extreme coercive measure that moderates reject.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: An absolutist libertarian principle; moderates accept force by the state in some cases.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist framing is not moderate, though moderates value markets; split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Moderates reject extremism and many accept defensive democracy, though they split on banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican concept not tied to moderation; split.

separated-powers.rationale: Aristotle's middle constitution and moderate political thought favor institutional balance and checks among the parts of the state.

vanguard-party.rationale: An extreme revolutionary doctrine that moderates reject.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Centrists back welfare programs but accommodate all sides rather than giving first priority to one group; split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A national policy issue with no moderate position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Centrists accommodate both labor and business, so restrictions on strikes get no consistent answer.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: A one-factor explanation, whereas moderates are pragmatic and avoid single-cause accounts; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: A divisive claim that moderates lean against; inferred from rejecting extremes.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Moderates prefer established elective institutions; lottery is a radical departure.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Suspending legal protections is an extreme measure that moderates reject, though some accept limited emergency powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Moderates accept market intervention in emergencies but not as doctrine; split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Government control of media contradicts the pluralist, multi-party system centrists operate in.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army is a one-party-state feature that centrists reject.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Moderates are divided on immigration policy.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A radical egalitarian measure not typical of moderates.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Moderates value compromise across party lines, so binding discipline gets no clear stance.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Centrists are described as typically supporting European integration and were central to building the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrating military and ministerial power in the head of state cuts against moderate balance of powers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: An internal church governance matter with no moderate position.

clerical-rule.rationale: Theocracy is an extreme that moderates reject.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is an extreme position that moderates reject.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moderates generally reject censorship on moral grounds as extreme, though some accept limited censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Unlimited tenure weakens institutional checks that moderates favor.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Ending permanent alliances is a radical shift, and moderates generally support established alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning rentals is a radical measure that moderates reject.

people-in-arms.rationale: Replacing a professional army is a radical change moderates oppose.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: A cultural assertion with no moderate position.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Dependent on context; moderates have no stated position.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: A populist claim; centrist populism exists but mainstream moderates tend not to adopt it.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Moderates are split between relativist and universalist views.

death-penalty.rationale: Moderates are divided on the death penalty.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Moderates lean toward including sex education, but the point is contested.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Moderates generally favor mainstream science curricula, inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: No moderate position; split on state restrictions.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Moderates vary by country and have no common stance.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Moderates are divided between accommodation and uniform law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's view; moderates are split between valuing tradition and individuality.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Cancelling debts is a sweeping measure that moderates mostly avoid, inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A radical economic transformation claim that moderates generally avoid.

constituent-assembly.rationale: No moderate stance; moderates prefer gradual change within existing constitutions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Restricting political freedoms is an authoritarian measure that moderates reject.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: A mild positive is inferred from moderate acceptance of welfare and international cooperation.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Defense policy with no moderate position.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Moderates have no stance; institutional preference varies by country.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Third Way and centrist politics are associated with fiscal and monetary stability, so independence is likely accepted, inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Moderates favor compromise, which suggests accepting territorial concessions for peace, inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Aristotle's mean treats property moderately, but modern moderates have no stated answer.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: An internal left debate; moderates hold no position.

precautionary-principle.rationale: No stated moderate position; moderates favor prudence but also weigh costs.

collective-defense.rationale: Centrists have supported Western institutions and alliances, inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Moderates generally uphold international norms against annexation, inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Historic liberal centrism opposed clericalism, but curbing property and clergy is more radical.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A moderate preference for standing above party conflict is inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine rulers are an extreme that moderates reject.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No stated moderate stance; compromise-oriented but not documented.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Centrists accept some redistribution through taxation, which a flat rate gives up; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: A nature-nurture question with no moderate position.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Centrism works through multi-party coalitions and institutions, incompatible with a ruler above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: No moderate stance on space policy.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Aristotle in Politics IV favors the mean, a constitution blending oligarchy and democracy resting on the middle class, a central source for political moderation.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader cults are an extreme that moderates reject.

equal-parenting.rationale: No moderate position on family-court presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine that moderates reject as extreme.

land-redistribution.rationale: Forced redistribution of estates is a radical measure; moderates favor gradual reform.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy is a religious extreme that moderates reject.

women-must-cover.rationale: A coercive religious rule that moderates reject.

common-currency.rationale: Centrists have backed European integration, but moderates differ on the euro.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnolinguistic political unification is a radical project moderates avoid.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The sources on moderation say nothing about minority autonomy, and moderates differ by country on how far to grant it.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Moderates reject economic determinism, preferring pragmatic politics of both ideas and interests.

ban-cartels.rationale: Centrist market-friendly policy with fair competition rules is documented for social market economies; inferred for moderates.

no-bailouts.rationale: Moderates are split between market discipline and stability.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Moderate thought favors balance and checks among institutions against unconstrained majorities.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: A third-way blend of open trade with social protection, inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives is a radical utopian measure moderates reject.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Guerrilla revolutionism is an extreme that moderates reject.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Moderates are found in both monarchies and republics; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Moderation as documented is silent on history teaching, and moderates split between national-centered and broader curricula.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial tutelage is widely rejected, including by moderates; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Moderates are divided between civic patriotism and critical approaches.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Moderates are split on affirmative action.

public-money-creation.rationale: A radical monetary reform beyond centrist views.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Centrism's mixed-economy outlook accepts that capitalism can be reformed rather than collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Nothing in the moderate sources addresses post-imperial influence, so adherents are treated as split on it.

delink-world-market.rationale: Delinking is a radical economic proposal that moderates reject.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory rejecting the class-collaboration approach of centrists.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A libertarian extreme that moderates generally reject, though some value freedom of association.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Institutional checks and a constitutional balance fit the moderate preference for the mean and stability.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The moderate sources do not discuss colonial boundary treaties, and moderates would likely split between legal continuity and redress.

elective-rulers.rationale: Centrism is a feature of democratic party systems with elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Individual vetoes defeat the compromise and coalition-building moderates favor.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Moderates generally prefer legal means; no stated position on resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Moderates are split on parliamentary sovereignty versus separated powers.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: A mainstream view moderates would accept, inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A middle position between abolition and unrestricted use, inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristotle treats the middle class as the stable core and the extremes of wealth as problematic, so moderates accept obligations among classes; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Moderates are participants in compromise politics, so withdrawal is unlikely.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School critique not associated with moderates.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim with no moderate stance.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is a radical analysis; centrists favor market integration.

native-born-offices.rationale: A restrictive nativist rule that moderates generally reject.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist matter with no moderate stance.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not part of the moderate canon; moderates would mix aid, trade and domestic effort, so no lean is given.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is an extreme position that moderates reject.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: A radical hierarchy of political authority by descent that moderates reject.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Moderates accept anti-extremism but split on constitutional wording.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Moderation is defined by rejecting extremes on both sides, which supports condemning both.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Historical consensus holds slavery was the main cause; moderates reject this revisionist claim.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Moderates are split; no stated stance.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Moderates may accept varied institutions or defend universal democratic norms, and the sources give no common answer.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political role for armed forces conflicts with democratic centrism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Moderation as a stance has no doctrine on unpaid household labor, and moderates divide on state payment for it.

filial-duty.rationale: A cultural and family-ethics question outside the moderate sources, on which moderates hold varied views.

office-by-exam.rationale: The sources on moderation do not address civil-service selection, and moderates have no shared view on exams versus election or patronage.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Moderates split between openness and protection.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Moderates generally accept no-fault divorce, inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates conflict with the moderate favoring of compromise by representatives.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Centrists support welfare-state programs; replacing pay-as-you-go with private accounts is more radical.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Abolishing private land ownership is an extreme that moderates reject.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Moderates support institutional balance and checks on executive power.

single-official-language.rationale: Moderates generally avoid coercive linguistic uniformity.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: A restrictive nativist measure moderates are unlikely to adopt broadly.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Neither the moderate nor centrist sources take a stance on consumer culture, so moderates are treated as split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: A risky interventionist tactic that moderates generally avoid.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: An imperial coercive doctrine that moderates reject.

corporate-influence.rationale: Moderates are split on lobbying and campaign finance.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Moderates weigh sovereignty against open civil society, and the sources give no shared position on funding limits.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not a defining moderate topic, and moderates differ on family subsidies versus immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: A restrictive measure moderates are unlikely to adopt.

job-guarantee.rationale: An expansive state measure beyond standard centrist welfare programs.

democratic-peace.rationale: Centrists are associated with democratic institutions and cooperation, so a mild agreement is inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Moderates are institutionalists who work within the political system and respect law.

non-intervention.rationale: Moderates avoid absolute positions, so a ban on all intervention is rejected.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is a labor-movement matter outside the moderate sources, so no moderate position is inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy claim that moderates reject as extreme.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: A radical proposal that moderates reject.

public-access-to-information.rationale: A mainstream good-government position moderates accept, inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anti-party organization is an anarchist doctrine moderates reject; they work through parties.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is an economic and green program item with no moderate stance in the sources.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the nation by religion is an exclusive extreme that moderates reject.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary diplomacy is not a moderate view of equal states.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal sharing between regions varies by country and the moderate sources offer no common position.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist distinction; moderates have no stance.

defeat-communism.rationale: Moderates are split between containment and coexistence.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Third Way and centrist politics blend market and social programs, with mixed providers in a publicly funded system.

religion-illusion.rationale: A strong atheist claim; moderates avoid ideological dogmatism on religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Centrists accept market capitalism blended with social programs, so mild agreement is inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Moderates favor reform within existing institutions, not system transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Moderates support families and some services but not public replacement of home care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is an extreme that moderates avoid.

cooperative-communities.rationale: A utopian reorganization that moderates reject.

treaties-binding.rationale: Moderates favor honoring agreements but also negotiated compromise; with no source on this question they are treated as split.

majority-settlement.rationale: An ethnic engineering policy that moderates reject.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Moderation is described as an ideology of the middle or third way, but a mixed-economy moderate need not call it a third system; split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Moderates generally favor compromise over historical claims, inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial of an established historical fact is an extreme that moderates reject.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: A repressive position that moderates reject.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Centrism depends on a multi-party system and compromise, incompatible with suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Punishing blasphemy is a religious extreme that moderates reject.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: A colonial exploitative stance that moderates reject.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A militant religious doctrine that moderates reject.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: An extreme militant doctrine that moderates reject.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Moderates accept participation but favor representative institutions; split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: This is an academic framework with no moderate doctrine, and moderates divide on whether to address oppressions together.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Moderates are split on this question.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Third Way leaders described their approach as neither left nor right and radical centrism combines the best ideas of each.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist claim moderates do not share, as they accept capitalism with reforms.

islam-incompatible.rationale: A sweeping claim about a religion that moderates reject as extreme.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Centrism is tied to democratic systems; moderate believers may hold it privately but not as a political premise.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A mainstream reform that moderates would accept, inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Centrism is associated with welfare-state programs and Third Way blending of markets with social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: An extreme position that moderates reject.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Moderate sources give no foreign policy stance on bloc membership, and moderates differ by country on alliances.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Moderates are found in monarchies and republics; no stance.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A monetary reform outside moderate thinking, rejected as radical.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Third Way associates with balanced budgets and prudence, so defying lenders is unlikely.

property-franchise.rationale: Aristotle's polity favors a broad middle class, not exclusion of the poor, and moderates accept universal suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist theory not typical of moderates.

reification.rationale: A Marxist critique moderates do not share.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A radical critique of liberal freedoms that moderates reject.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Moderate constitutionalism favors law over arbitrary rule, in line with Aristotle's middle constitution.

racial-franchise.rationale: An extreme racist position that moderates reject.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is not addressed in the moderate sources, and moderates have no shared view on it.

open-government-data.rationale: A good-government position moderates accept, inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: An illiberal measure that moderates reject.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: A sectarian discrimination tactic that moderates reject.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claiming foreign territory by nationality is an extreme irredentist position that moderates reject.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic closed blocs are an extreme, at odds with the market-friendly centrism described by Third Way politics.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Moderates are split on how to frame gender disadvantage; no stated position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: No moderate stance; contested research and policy question.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Moderates favour deliberation and compromise across the spectrum, which a lot-chosen assembly embodies, but they also trust representative institutions; inferred from the compromise method, not stated in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Moderates favour gradual adaptation over fixed inherited doctrine, but the sources never address religious reform and this is inferred from their reformist temperament.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Moderates split between worry about inequality and defence of market outcomes; the sources give no position on wealth and liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Polling and centrist practice in many countries now accept open service, but moderates vary by country and generation, so only a mild lean is inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Moderation rejects radical programmes, and state-imposed atheism is one; moderates favour a neutral state.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Abolition is a radical position that moderation by definition rejects; moderates favour reform of policing at most.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The scholarship on moderation stresses compromise and coalition in deep conflicts, which fits power-sharing; this is inferred, not stated for the generic stance.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Moderates accept a mixed welfare state but disagree about the role of charity; no source gives a position.

term-limits.rationale: Not tied to moderation as a stance; moderates are split and the sources are silent.

vote-delegation.rationale: Moderates favour representative institutions and gradual change over novel direct-democracy schemes; inferred, not documented.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Moderation says nothing on this; adherents divide between present-focused pragmatism and long-term prudence.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Moderates vary by religious tradition and country, and the sources do not address religious office.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Moderates in most countries accept equality between spouses as mainstream, but the stance is positional so this is inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Moderates split on immigrant political rights, and the sources do not address it, so no lean is inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Centrists accept a mixed economy but divide on market regulation of housing; this is inferred from that split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Moderates keep the market framework of a mixed economy, which includes property rights in inventions; inferred, not stated.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Moderation rejects radical and extreme movements, and drilled mass youth organisations are typical of ideological extremes; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Moderates hold no common line on nuclear basing; it divides along party and national lines.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Centrists generally support alliances and European integration (s2), which often involve hosting allied forces; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Mainstream centrists support formal acknowledgement of historical crimes, though positions vary by country; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Support for a welfare state and mixed economy implies rewarding work over idle ownership, but moderates do not frame it this way; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Most moderates accept the legitimacy of force in defence of self and others, as in mainstream law; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Moderation favours pragmatism over mythic national narratives, so strong continuity claims are unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The moderate mainstream is not radical on gender theory and tends to treat sex as biological; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Moderates are split on identity-based feminist theory; no stated position.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Moderates are wary of cults of sacrifice and extreme nationalism, though many honour war dead in ordinary ways; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Moderation is defined against absolutist, good-versus-evil framings of politics and favours compromise (s1, s2); inferred from that.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Moderates do not address diaspora and homeland questions as a bloc.

culture-before-state.rationale: Moderates see the state and its institutions as the ordinary frame for reform, not cultural revival as a prior project; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Moderates divide on religious language; religious and secular centrists both exist.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Moderates divide on feminist critique of religion; no common stance.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Moderates support democratic institutions and equal citizenship (s1, s2), which rule out ethnic dominance of the economy; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Gradualist moderates favour compromise over redrawing administrative borders by ethnic lines; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Centrist parties accept independent unions within a pluralist democracy; inferred from that, as the sources do not address unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Moderates reject class-based claims about who must hold power and accept democratic mixed-economy politics as sufficient; inferred from centrism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Centrist mixed-economy welfare politics tolerates public provision of local essentials; inferred, and moderates vary by country.

second-chamber.rationale: Aristotle's mixed constitution and the Whig and Doctrinaire tradition favour balancing institutions such as a second chamber; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Moderates accept private ownership alongside the state and avoid radical communal ownership; inferred from rejection of extremes.

confederal-coordination.rationale: A programme of confederal municipal rule with no governing centre is a radical structural scheme moderates do not take up; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Moderates are split on wage policy and family structure, and no source addresses it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Moderation is a method, not a programme, and moderates divide on regulatory speed versus caution.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: No source places moderates on ageing research, and attitudes vary by country and party.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Moderates divide between civil-liberty and law-enforcement concerns on financial privacy; no source settles it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Moderates broadly back liberal-democratic civil liberties, though they also accept some regulation; a mild inference.

person-over-state.rationale: Liberal-democratic centrism holds that the state serves individuals, though the sources do not state it; inferred at low confidence.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Moderates are split between secular and religious outlooks, so no stance is documented.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Moderates vary by country between unitary and federal arrangements; no common position.

gm-crops.rationale: No source addresses agricultural technology, and moderates hold mixed views.

dense-cities.rationale: Environmental and urban policy is not a moderate-defining issue and positions vary.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Moderates reject identity-based extreme politics and favour compromise across groups; inferred from that rejection.

racial-pride.rationale: Moderates split on identity questions of this kind and the sources do not address it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Moderates take mixed views on the use of force, varying by country and issue.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Moderates favor pragmatic civic national belonging and distrust identity absolutes; the stance is positional, so this is inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Moderates stress compromise within shared institutions, and communal separation tends toward polarization; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Moderation means weighing evidence on each issue, which counts against conspiracy claims; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Moderates favor a mixed welfare state but tend to resist fully free provision as too programmatic; this is a contested inference.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Centrist and Third Way strands accept market-based environmental charges as a pragmatic middle course; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Gradual reform and prudence imply care for the long term; the sources do not state it, so it is inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Moderates do not generally hold that women bring distinct values deserving extra weight; positional and inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Reducing armaments to what safety requires is a typical middle position between disarmament and militarism; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Moderates divide between valuing transparency and valuing discreet diplomacy; no stated position.

capital-controls.rationale: Moderates in mixed economies usually accept open capital markets with moderate regulation; contested and inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the moderate support for stable democratic institutions and order; moderates vary by country.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from moderation's respect for institutions and order; it is not a stated position.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the mixed economy and welfare-state compromise typical of moderates, though views vary.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the Third Way and centrist support for work-based welfare.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from the centrist habit of combining fiscal prudence with a welfare state; moderates divide on this.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Moderates are split between gradual reform of international rules and keeping them; the label fixes no position.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Moderation is defined by rejecting radical or extreme methods and favouring gradual reform within existing institutions.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the preference for a mixed economy over any single system; not stated.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Moderates divide on pricing nature; the stance is about method and fixes no view.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from moderation's distrust of fervent, absolute commitments; nationalism varies by country.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Moderates are split on student debt relief, and the label fixes no position.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the preference for gradualism and the lack of a radical structural critique.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the moderate acceptance of liberal-democratic rights, which rest on common human dignity.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the mixed-economy and compromise tradition, which accepts public funding of common goods.

missingStatements.text: Political disputes should be settled by compromise rather than by either side getting everything it wants.
missingStatements.rationale: Compromise and accommodation of both sides are the defining method of moderates and centrist parties.

missingStatements.text: The most stable political order rests on a large middle class rather than on the very rich or the very poor.
missingStatements.rationale: Aristotle's Politics IV argues that the mean condition and a numerous middle class are free from faction and make the best state.

notes: Moderation is a positional and methodological label, so most substantive policy answers are low-confidence and many are neutral: self-described moderates divide on healthcare, guns, drugs, immigration and abortion. Medium answers mostly follow from rejecting radical or extreme proposals and from documented centrist support for gradualism, a mixed economy and democratic coalition politics.
